text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects the government of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to turn words into deeds. Next year inflation should not exceed a monthly 2.5 percent.
- The government plans to liberalise prices by the end of next August.
ADEVARUL
- High inflation and a bulky state budget deficit are among the carryovers from the former government.
- The leu's exchange rate has frozen at around 4,800 to the dollar on both the interbank market and at retail currency shops for several days.
ZIUA
- A government statement shows that the IMF gave Romania a period of grace of four months to put together an economic programme.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- If the Ciorbea cabinet accepts the conditions imposed by the IMF Romanians are going to face an explosion of prices in the immediately following period.
LIBERTATEA

- The rise in the price of petrol planned for Janaury, along with a depreciated leu will have a direct impact on Romanians' thin wallets, the newspaper says, adding that queues at filling stations have already swollen.
- The price of ARO four-wheel-drive cars is expected to rise by 11.8 perrcent starting January.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Bids from foreign investors for stakes in Romanian companies currently amount to $400 million, the State Ownership Fund said recently.
- The government pledges to cut subsidies to half in eight months' time.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Cars queue on several kilometres at the Hungarian- Romanian border.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- President Emil Constantinescu meets editors-in-chief of central dailies on Tuesday to discuss the problems facing Romania.
- Monday's editorial demands Constantinescu to unmask the huge corruption behind most of the country's newly rich.
- Virgil Magureanu, the head of Romanian Intelligence Service, called for a merger of all anti-terrorist services in Romania.
LIBERTATEA
- Caricaturist Mihai Stanescu wrapped the government building in a huge red ribbon ahead of Christmas Holidays.

- More than 50 percent of the young people up to 30 years of age do not earn enough to live decently, the Youth Studies Centre showed in a survey. It shows 44 percent of young married couples live with their parents as they cannot afford a house.
ADEVARUL
- Peter Buchwald, nominated for the job of deputy-prefect in the Transylvanian county of Cluj, said he would introduce Hungarian as an alternative official language in public administration.
- Local governments will be given autonomy and the move is expected to solve the problems of both the Romanian majority and the Hungarian ethnic minority, Constantinescu said in interview.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Some 60,000 cases of influenza were registered in the past two weeks in Romania. ($= 3,914 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
